national.title: U.S. national dental spending, utilization and out-of-pocket burden (MEPS)
national.source: AHRQ Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), Household Component
caveats: MEPS measures person-level spending and utilization, not per-procedure prices; do not compare these figures with CDT-code benchmarks.
Year-over-year deltas are point-estimate differences without survey variance estimation (no VARSTR/VARPSU standard errors computed); treat small changes as indicative only.
Expenditures = amounts actually paid (all payers); charges = billed amounts before adjustment.
The 2023-2024 differences in this file are not confirmed by the paired Panel 28 longitudinal estimates (see /api/v1/meps/longitudinal.json); no national trend should be inferred.

longitudinal.title: U.S. dental spending and utilization, same persons 2023 to 2024 (MEPS Panel 28 longitudinal)
longitudinal.source: AHRQ Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), Household Component
caveats: All dollar amounts are nominal (2023 and 2024 dollars as reported), not inflation-adjusted.

The longitudinal population (persons in scope the whole 2023-2024 period) is NOT the same universe as the annual cross-sections in data/meps-national.json; levels are expected to differ (newborns, immigrants, deaths and institutionalized persons are treated differently).
MEPS measures person-level spending and utilization, not per-procedure prices; do not compare these figures with CDT-code benchmarks.
Expenditures = amounts actually paid (all payers); out-of-pocket = self/family payments; Medicaid amount = payments reported as made by Medicaid.
Changes whose 95pct confidence interval contains 0 are not statistically distinguishable from no change; the sign of such a change carries no information.
Self-reported dental expenditures are subject to reporting error; Medicaid payment amounts are known to be under-reported in household surveys.
These are figures only; no causal or policy interpretation is attached to them.
longitudinal.reading: The differences between the two annual cross-sections (HC-256 minus HC-251) are not confirmed by the paired Panel 28 estimates: no paired change in spending, out-of-pocket or Medicaid-paid amounts is statistically significant at the 95 percent level. We therefore report no national 2023-2024 trend in either direction. The cross-sectional differences carry their own sampling error, which data/meps-national.json does not estimate.
